first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction improve time-to-value and first-week activation. Verify the two most directly relevant records before committing. Use a standard experiment rather than broad rollout to confirm the effects in the current environment and monitor downstream qualified revenue and retention. Avoid promotional pricing because prior evidence shows acquisition lift accompanied by materially worse 30-day retention.

final.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-shortening experiment this week, prioritizing the observed completion and time-to-value decline. The verified result improved completion, time-to-value, adoption, and 30-day retention, making it the strongest sustainable qualified-revenue opportunity. Signup simplification may support SMB activation, but its slight retention decline and limited segment generalization argue against making it the primary intervention. Measure activation, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention by segment before rollout.
